newsitem.title: ITALY: POLL-Italy seen offering 13trln lire paper at sale.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Italy seen offering 13trln lire paper at sale.

text.p: Italy is expected to offer around 13.0 trillion lire of medium to long term paper at its end of month auctions, of which around 2.5 trillion is forecast to be at a variable rate, analysts said on Thursday.
Forecasts from seven analysts polled by Reuters ranged from a total of 10.5 trillion to 16.0 trillion lire of paper.

Some 19.5 trillion lire of three-year fixed-rate government bonds (Btps) are expiring along with 1.45 trillion of floating rate certificates (CCTs), while 19.3 trillion lire worth of Btp coupons fall due.
Economists said they expected the Italian Treasury to aim for a substantial issue of 10-year paper, which is now only on offer in the turn-of-month auction rather than the midmonth sale.
The Treasury auctions the 11th tranche of May 1, 2004 CCTs carrying a first coupon of 3.45 percent, on July 30, along with the third tranche of January 1, 2007 Btps, bearing a coupon of 6.75 percent.
The following day the Treasury then auctions an 11th tranche of the May 15, 2000 Btp, with a coupon of 6.0 percent, and the ninth tranche of the May 15, 2002 Btp with a 6.25 percent coupon.
The Ministry will announce the quantities on Friday.
